content: The Gull's Maw was a subterranean sea cavern carved into the basalt roots of the island. At low tide, black volcanic sand emerged between jagged pillars of glistening slate. The cavern echoed with the deep, booming roar of Atlantic swells breaking against the outer reef, smelling of rotting kelp, brine, and cold, refined machine oil.
critique: Sanderson: Strong biological limits and mechanical vector precision.
